about: The listing on the Winter Haven Community Calendar is titled Tree Lighting Ceremony and calls it the Annual Tree Lighting Celebration. It gives Thursday, December 3, 2026, from 6 PM to 7:30 PM and a cost of Free.

Around Winter Haven, a local guide to Polk County holiday events, describes it as a City of Winter Haven and Main Street Winter Haven tradition. The guide says live entertainment begins at 6 PM and the tree lights at 7 PM.

The calendar places the event in Central Park on 4th Street Northwest and names no Santa or kid activities. Think of it as a community gathering around the tree, with the entertainment starting at 6 PM.

Nearby, the city calendar also lists Holidays on Central on December 5 and Winter Haven Winter Wonderland on December 11, so the tree lighting is the first of three city-hosted Christmas dates in this park.
The calendar entry shows a 6 PM start and a 7:30 PM end, a short program that fits a school night. The page title is simply Tree Lighting Ceremony, and the host is the city's own community calendar.
The tree is lit at 7 PM per the local guide, so the final half hour is for photos in front of the lit tree. Stay put if you want that picture with the lights on.
Thursday evening timing matters for families with school the next morning. With a 7:30 PM finish, you can see the tree lit and still be home at a reasonable hour.
Winter Haven also lists a holiday movie matinee, The Polar Express, on December 19 at 2 PM at the public library, which pairs well with this free tree lighting if you want more than one night out.
The Winter Haven calendar groups the tree lighting with other city programming, and the Polk County guide lists it among its season of parades, Santa sightings and concerts.
Anyone coming from out of town can combine the evening with the library matinee of The Polar Express on December 19, which the same calendar lists.

about: The city calendar lists Winter Haven Winter Wonderland for Friday, December 11, 2026, from 6 PM to 9 PM in Central Park and describes it as a free community celebration for the whole family.

Four activities are named: a holiday movie under the stars, inflatables, local food trucks and holiday crafts. The page does not say which movie is playing, so check the city calendar closer to the date.
Santa photos run 6:30 PM to 8:30 PM, a two hour window inside a three hour evening. Families who want a photo and a spot for the movie can do the photo line first.
This is the city's third Central Park holiday date in 2026, after the December 3 tree lighting and the Holidays on Central festival on December 5.
Because the movie plays outdoors, most families bring a blanket, a folding chair or both. The host listing does not require tickets or registration, and it gives the cost as Free.
The calendar lists it as a free city celebration. It falls a week after the Havendale parade and the boat parade weekend, which makes December 11 a good option if you missed those.
Crafts and inflatables are aimed at younger children, while the movie works for all ages. The listing calls it festive fun for the whole family.
Plan the evening in this order: arrive around 6 PM for crafts and the bounce houses, take the Santa photo between 6:30 and 8:30 PM, then settle in with a snack from a food truck for the film.
The Winter Haven Chamber listing for Holidays on Central on December 5 mentions free Santa photos, so Winter Wonderland is the second chance to get a picture with him in Central Park.

about: Visit Central Florida describes the Winter Haven Chain of Lakes Christmas Boat Parade as an annual event on the lakes, and says it begins promptly at 6:30 PM on Saturday, December 5, 2026. The page lists no ticket price, and it is a public parade, so we show it as free.
The listed route is Lake May to Lake Howard, back to Lake May, then onto Lake Shipp. That loop means boats pass the same stretch of shoreline more than once.
The page names Harborside Restaurant, Tanner's Lakeside Bar and Grill, Old Man Franks and the Twisted Prop as viewing areas, without street addresses.
A Polk County holiday guide lists the parade as 6:30 PM to 8:30 PM. Because it is after dark, it pairs with the Havendale Christmas Parade the night before on December 4 for a parade weekend.
The Visit Central Florida page was updated on October 27, 2026, and gives December 5 as the date, so the listing is for this season and not an older year.

Winter Haven is known for its chain of lakes, and the parade is built around three of them: May, Howard and Shipp. Kids who like boats and lights get a view from the shoreline without buying a ticket.
faq: When is the boat parade?
Saturday, December 5, 2026, beginning promptly at 6:30 PM.
What is the route?
Lake May to Lake Howard, back to Lake May, then Lake Shipp.
Where can we watch?
The listing names Harborside Restaurant, Tanner's Lakeside Bar and Grill, Old Man Franks and the Twisted Prop.

The listing gives no price. Watching a public parade from the shore is normally free.
Are there street addresses?
The page does not list them, so look each venue up before you drive.
Can we watch from the shore?
The listing points to waterfront restaurants as viewing areas, so shoreline spots near them are the places to start.
What time should we arrive?
The parade begins promptly at 6:30 PM, so arrive before then.
Which lakes does it cover?
Lake May, Lake Howard and Lake Shipp.

about: The Winter Haven Community Calendar lists the Havendale Christmas Parade on Friday, December 4, 2026, from 7 PM to 9 PM. The route runs about 3.1 miles along Havendale Boulevard.
It starts near 14th Street and Havendale Boulevard in Winter Haven and continues west toward Auburndale, ending just before 42nd Street. That is a long route, so you can choose a spot close to home.
The only price on the page is a registration fee of $50 per unit, which applies to groups entering the parade. Spectators are not charged on the listing, and we show the parade as free.
A local Polk County guide also lists this parade on December 4 at 7 PM, the night before the Chain of Lakes Christmas Boat Parade and Holidays on Central on December 5.

The route follows Havendale Boulevard NW and crosses toward the Auburndale side of Winter Haven, which makes it a neighborhood parade rather than a downtown one. The calendar entry gives the stretch as roughly three miles.
Bring layers and a chair. The listing does not describe floats, bands or Santa, so check the host page for entries as the date gets closer.
The listing gives no road closure or parking notes. If you are heading to the 7 PM start, plan to park on a side street and walk to the route.

Friday, December 4, 2026, from 7 PM to 9 PM.
